chapter: The avant garde, race and the artist's voice
title: The Malcolm X opera and The Meeting
summary: Baker passed on a Malcolm X opera for time reasons but found the two-man play The Meeting between Malcolm and King attractive.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: I know at one point you were approached about writing an opera based on the life of Malcolm X. Then at one point, too, a project was proposed to you which I found very interesting, the project called The Meeting.

We talked earlier about the Malcolm project. I didn’t do that simply because it would have made an encroachment on my time that I was unwilling to give. The Meeting was a little more impressive to me. Sam Floyd sent me a copy of the video that was a mythical meeting between Malcolm X and Martin Luther King. It was going to be a two-man play. They talked about their differences, but their commonalties. I was approached, and I found that very exciting, to write an opera, a two-person opera based on that. I have no notion why it dissipated. Perhaps because nobody bugged me. I never did follow through on it. It’s something that I still find attractive and something that I think would be very good, just like I think Anthony Davis’s opera X was very, very effective. I think, again, we respond to time and place.
